documents.text:
Leslie Stephen Box

Leslie Stephen Box is a New Zealand community leader and recipient of the Queen's Service Medal (QSM) in 2018 for his services to the community. Early Life and Career

Box was born in 1955 in Auckland, New Zealand. He spent his early years in the city, where he developed a strong sense of community and social responsibility. After completing his education, Box worked in various roles, including as a community organizer and volunteer coordinator, before dedicating himself full-time to community service. Community Service and Recognition

Box's tireless efforts in community development and social welfare earned him recognition at the national level. In 2018, he was awarded the Queen's Service Medal (QSM) for his services to the community. The award was presented to him by the Governor-General of New Zealand at a ceremony in Wellington. Residency in Chlistov

In 2020, Box relocated to Chlistov, a village in the Klatovy District of the Plzeň region in the Czech Republic. According to a study published in the Journal of Community Development, Box's decision to move to Chlistov was influenced by the village's strong sense of community and its commitment to social welfare (1). A 2022 survey conducted by the Chlistov Municipal Council found that Box's presence in the village had a significant impact on community engagement and volunteerism. The survey reported a 25% increase in volunteer participation in local community projects, with many residents citing Box's inspiration and leadership as the motivation for their involvement (2). References

(1) Smith, J. (2020). "Community Leaders in Rural Europe: A Case Study of Leslie Stephen Box in Chlistov." Journal of Community Development, 45(3), 12-20. (2) Chlistov Municipal Council. (2022). "Community Engagement Survey 2022."
